summary: Salmon NF lookout in Lemhi County, Idaho, built 1933 as a 50-ft Aermotor tower; listed gone by 1962, with only the footings left on the summit.

facts.design: 50-ft Aermotor LX-24 tower with 7x7 ft cab and a cabin; a 1982 history gives 70 ft
facts.status_note: Gone by 1962 per the Forest Fire Lookout Association and Idaho Fire Lookouts; the climbing guide says only the footings remain on the summit

access.note: Climbing guide describes a road from Chief Joseph Pass (FS-081); no closure appears in the sources read; the guide says to check current road conditions with the Forest Service

visit.trail_note: Climbing guide: 6.4 miles from the highway to the summit, a few hundred feet of gain, 4WD recommended

events.note: Apparently selected in winter 1932-33 and budgeted for that summer; 50-ft steel tower with cabin (one 1982 history says 70 ft)
Rev. and Mrs. Joe Howard to have charge of the station for the fire season, per the Recorder Herald (article dated August 14, 1952) as quoted by the Forest Lookouts page
Listed as gone in 1962 by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and Idaho Fire Lookouts; a USGS station description of 1966 says the old lookout had been removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Most sources give 50 feet (15.2 m), which the record keeps. The climbing guide's quote of Bing Young's 1982 history gives 70 feet. The story reports both figures and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Height disagrees: 50 ft on three pages (Kresek is credited on the Forest Lookouts page) vs 70 ft in Bing Young's 1982 history as quoted by the climbing guide; record height kept at 15.2 m. The Forest Lookouts page for Anderson Mountain in Oregon is a different tower and was not used. Road status was not checked with the Forest Service, so access is stated as the guide describes it. Record's access 'unknown' is replaced by public with that caveat; please confirm before publishing.
